name: Prime Agent
tagline: A self-improving RLM agent for coding workflows and long-running autonomous tasks
description: Prime Agent is an open-source coding and research agent built for general-purpose and long-running work. It is designed around two core abstractions: a Recursive Language Model (RLM) that treats context as variables (prompt-as-a-variable) and tools such as recursive subagents as function calls inside a persistent REPL, and a Continual Harness that stores durable state — supplemental prompts, memories, skill descriptions, and reusable subagent specifications — as lightweight, evidence-backed updates that the agent can refine over time. The agent ships with a terminal UI, daemon-backed continuity for detached sessions, direct agent-to-agent messaging, persistent goals, and a bounded autonomous mode with configurable turn, token, and time budgets plus optional quality gates. It is published under the MIT License.
highlights: Recursive Language Model with prompt-as-a-variable and programmatic subagent calling
Continual Harness persists memories, skills, and subagent specs as durable state
Daemon-backed continuity keeps sessions, IPython state, and subagents alive after detach
Direct agent-to-agent messaging and persistent /goal tracking across turns
Bounded autonomous mode with turn, token, and time budgets plus user-defined quality gates
curatorNote: Prime Intellect's open, self-improving coding agent — a serious RLM take on long-running autonomous work, currently at roughly 8.2k stars.
